babson-academy-summer-study-2027.about:
Babson Academy Summer Study is an intensive three-week pre-college programme (12–30 July 2027) built on Babson College's Entrepreneurial Thought & Action methodology. All students take the Babson College course EPS 1110 Introduction to the Entrepreneurial Experience, working in teams on real-world business challenges linked to the UN Global Goals: three hours a day in class plus about five hours of team and individual work (around 40 hours a week).

It runs in two formats: fully online (classes 8–11 a.m. ET) or in person, hosted by the New England Innovation Academy (NEIA) in Massachusetts, with double-occupancy en-suite dorms, 24/7 supervision, evening activities, a Babson campus tour, local sightseeing and NEIA's AI for Innovation programme. An information session for 2027 is on 8 December 2026.
highlights: Real Babson College entrepreneurship course
Online or residential with an AI-for-innovation strand
Need-based financial assistance with fee waiver
babson-academy-summer-study-2027.eligibility: Rising high-school juniors or seniors aged at least 15 by the start date (no exceptions). English proficiency required (minimum TOEFL 90 or equivalent IELTS, Duolingo or Cambridge score) unless English is the native language or the school's language of instruction. Open to students worldwide; a computer, webcam and reliable internet are required.
how_to_apply: Attend the information session (8 December 2026) and check the Key Dates tab
Complete part 1 of the Workday application and pay the USD 100 fee (waived if applying for need-based aid)
Complete part 2: school official uploads transcript; add English proficiency evidence and essays
Choose online or in-person (NEIA) format
babson-academy-summer-study-2027.costs: Paid programme; tuition for online and in-person formats is listed under 'Program Cost & Aid' on the Babson page. USD 100 application fee (waived for financial-aid applicants). Need-based financial assistance available.

bentley-pre-college-2027.about:
Bentley University, a business university in Waltham near Boston, runs one-week pre-college courses for high-school students from 7 June to 23 July 2027. The 2027 schedule includes the Wall Street 101 series (Macroeconomics and Financial Markets, Stock Market and Investment Research, Trading Strategies, Global Finance and Trade, Personal Finance, FinTech Business Start-ups, several offered for credit), plus Data Analytics, Quant Risk Management, AI in Society, Pathways for Women in Math, Accounting Adventures, Social Entrepreneurship, and the business of sports, health, fashion and beauty. Courses run 9:00–17:00 with workshops, networking with Bentley students and faculty, and social outings.

Students aged 16 by 1 September can live in the residence halls (residential fee includes housing, meals, weekday activity transport and an airport shuttle); younger students can attend as commuters or take online Wall Street 101 courses. Applications open 15 January 2027 with rolling admission until 15 May. International students are welcome; those without two years of US high school must show English proficiency.
highlights: Hands-on finance, data analytics and quant courses
Residential option with airport shuttle; online option
Some Wall Street 101 courses earn college credit
bentley-pre-college-2027.eligibility: High-school students; must be 16 by 1 September 2027 to live on campus (younger students may commute or study online). Applicants who have not completed at least two years of US high school must demonstrate English proficiency. International students may apply (Bentley does not support visa applications; scholarships do not cover travel).
how_to_apply: Choose one or more 2027 sessions from the schedule
Create an account and apply online from 15 January 2027; pay the USD 75 application fee
Rolling admission until 15 May 2027; places are reserved only with full payment
Optionally request need-based scholarship (international students submit an extra financial form)
bentley-pre-college-2027.costs: 2026/27 listed tuition per 5-day course: online USD 1,490; commuter USD 2,450–2,800; residential USD 3,380–3,730 (housing, meals, activity transport and airport shuttle included). USD 75 application fee. Limited need-based scholarships (no travel funding).

exeter-college-oxford-summer-programme-2.about:
The Exeter College Summer Programme is run by Exeter College itself, one of the oldest colleges of the University of Oxford (founded 1314). From 27 June to 7 August 2027 students live in college (en-suite rooms at the modern Cohen Quadrangle or historic Turl Street) and take two cross-disciplinary lecture courses taught by leading scholars, with teaching modelled on Oxford's tutorial system of small, discussion-based groups. Students interested in specialist research, a senior thesis or graduate school can instead work one-to-one with an expert on an Independent Research Tutorial. Evening lectures, study-skills workshops, formal dinners and a daily social programme complete the experience, and a transcript is issued.

Applicants must be in full-time higher education, be 18 and have completed at least one year of undergraduate study by the start, with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.6/4.0 or equivalent. Admission is rolling and competitive. The college offers a small number of part-fee scholarships and bursaries for admitted students with outstanding records (GPA 3.8+) and financial need (deadline 22 February 2027).
highlights: Run by Exeter College, University of Oxford
Oxford tutorial-style teaching or 1-to-1 research tutorial
Part-fee scholarships and bursaries for strong students in need
exeter-college-oxford-summer-programme-2.eligibility: Full-time university students of any nationality, aged 18+, with at least one completed year of undergraduate study and a GPA of 3.6/4.0 or equivalent; non-native speakers at non-English-medium universities need an English certificate. Scholarships: GPA 3.8+ and financial need.
how_to_apply: Apply online (rolling) with transcript, academic reference, graded writing sample and English certificate if required; pay the GBP 60 application fee
Expect a decision within about a week
If admitted, apply for a scholarship/bursary by 22 February 2027 if eligible
Pay the programme fee by 13 June 2027 and apply for a UK visa or ETA
exeter-college-oxford-summer-programme-2.costs: 2027: application fee GBP 60; tuition GBP 4,495 (two courses, tutorials, academic support, transcript); accommodation GBP 4,355 (single en-suite room, weekday full board, formal dinners, social programme). Flights and insurance extra. Small number of part-fee scholarships/bursaries.

ictp-school-birational-enumerative-geome.about:
The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), a UNESCO Category 1 institute in Trieste, opens its 2027 Special Program 'Moduli Spaces: Geometry, Structures, and Invariants' with this school and workshop (15–26 February 2027). The first week has five minicourses by Michela Artebani, Izzet Coskun, Martijn Kool, Georg Oberdieck and Alessandra Sarti on central topics in moduli theory; the second week is a conference on recent results, with speakers from ETH Zurich, MIT, Yale, Edinburgh, Peking University and others.

It is aimed at PhD students, master's students in mathematics and early-career researchers in algebraic geometry. Applicants submit a short research abstract and may be selected for a poster or contributed talk. There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants (travel and/or subsistence) are available, with priority for participants from developing countries, which include Georgia; accommodation in ICTP guesthouses can be requested.
highlights: Leading algebraic geometers as lecturers
No registration fee; grants for developing-country participants
Poster or contributed-talk opportunity
ictp-school-birational-enumerative-geome.eligibility: Master's and PhD students and young researchers in mathematics (algebraic geometry) of any nationality; priority for financial support to applicants from developing countries (Georgia is eligible as a developing country under ICTP rules).
how_to_apply: Open the event page and click 'Apply here' (ICTP portal)
Fill in the form, upload CV and a short research abstract (ICTP template)
Request financial support and guesthouse accommodation in the form if needed, by 20 November 2026
Have a recommendation letter sent if requested
ictp-school-birational-enumerative-geome.costs: No registration fee. Limited ICTP grants cover travel and/or living costs for selected participants (priority to developing countries). Otherwise travel and accommodation are self-funded.

ictp-spring-college-physics-complex-syst.about:
ICTP and SISSA, with the partner universities of the International Master in Physics of Complex Systems and support from Politecnico di Torino and Capital Fund Management, run this Spring College from 15 February to 12 March 2027. It consists of four courses of nine lectures each, with a final exam per course: statistical physics of graphs and networks with applications to neuroscience (Raffaella Burioni), exact solutions of gradient flows in learning-theory models (Nicolas Macris, EPFL), non-equilibrium stochastic transport (Kirone Mallick and Izaak Neri) and the physics of cancer (Indian Institute of Science).

The college is part of the PCS master's programme and is open to qualified master's and PhD students and young researchers in physics and related fields. Applicants need recommendation letters from their supervisors and can submit a poster abstract. There is no registration fee; limited ICTP grants are available with priority for developing countries (Georgia qualifies). Grant holders must attend at least 80% of lectures and sit the exams; certificates require 80% attendance.
highlights: Four graduate courses with exams in 4 weeks
No fee; ICTP grants for developing-country students
Part of an international master's programme
ictp-spring-college-physics-complex-syst.eligibility: Master's and PhD students and young researchers in physics or related quantitative fields, any nationality; recommendation letter from supervisor required; priority for grants to applicants from developing countries (including Georgia).
how_to_apply: Apply on the ICTP portal via 'Apply here' on the event page by 1 November 2026
Upload CV and optional poster abstract (ICTP template)
Ask your supervisor to send a recommendation letter
Indicate if you need financial support
ictp-spring-college-physics-complex-syst.costs: No registration fee. Limited grants for travel and/or subsistence (priority to developing countries). Otherwise travel and accommodation self-funded.

rutgers-pre-college-summer-academies-202.about:
The Rutgers Pre-College Summer Academies are one-week, in-person residential programmes on the Rutgers–New Brunswick campus, designed for both US and international high-school (secondary-school) students. Each academy combines daily academic workshops, lectures, tours and activities led by Rutgers instructors with evening activities and events, under 24-hour supervision by programme and resident assistants. 2026 topics were Astronomy & Astrophysics, Engineering, Design Invent & Prototype, Physical Therapy (credit), Building Leadership Strategies (credit), Marketing & Product Innovation, College Readiness and Pre-Law & Mock Trial.

In 2026 academies ran in weeks between 12 July and 1 August; applications opened on 5 January, with an international deadline of 12 April. Class sizes are kept small. Students can attend more than one academy week (each charged separately).
highlights: Week-long residential academies incl. astronomy and engineering
Built for international as well as US students
Small classes and full residential supervision
rutgers-pre-college-summer-academies-202.eligibility: High-school students completing 10th or 11th grade, aged 16–18 (must be 16 before the summer), minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and English proficiency (recommended TOEFL 79, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 105; otherwise an interview may be arranged). International participants need an F-1 or J-1 visa arranged through Rutgers Global after admission and must buy health insurance.
how_to_apply: Check the Summer Academies Important Dates page for the 2027 cycle (opened 5 January in 2026)
Submit the online application with transcript and English proficiency evidence
International applicants: apply by the international deadline (12 April in 2026)
Once accepted, pay the USD 500 non-refundable deposit and complete visa documents with Rutgers Global
rutgers-pre-college-summer-academies-202.costs: 2026 total cost per one-week academy: USD 2,899 for non-credit academies (including housing and meals); credit academies USD 3,784–5,068 depending on residency status. USD 500 deposit counts toward the total. International students also pay visa, health-insurance and travel costs.

syracuse-summer-college-2027.about:
Syracuse University's Summer College lets high-school students take a real college-level course and experience university life. Summer College – On Campus is residential or commuter, lasting up to four weeks, with credit and noncredit courses across many subject areas, plus residence-hall life, dining-centre meals and campus activities. Summer College – Online offers 3-, 4- or 6-week credit and noncredit courses with virtual events, accessible from anywhere in the world.

Students who successfully complete credit courses earn a Syracuse University transcript. Between 2018 and 2022 participants came from 50 US states and territories and 55+ countries. In 2026 the application opened on 15 December 2025 and closed on 1 May 2026, with rolling decisions; international students taking credit courses on campus need an F-1 visa (I-20 issued about three weeks after the deposit).
highlights: Earn Syracuse University credit or try a noncredit course
Residential college experience or online from anywhere
Students from 55+ countries
syracuse-summer-college-2027.eligibility: Students aged 15+ by move-in. Noncredit courses: rising sophomores, juniors, seniors or recent graduates; credit courses: rising juniors, seniors or recent graduates. Non-native English speakers show proficiency (preferred TOEFL 85, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 105, or English-medium schooling). International students on campus taking credit courses need an F-1 visa (not B-1/B-2).
how_to_apply: Choose On Campus or Online and a course when the 2027 application opens (15 December in 2026)
Submit transcripts (at least one full year of grades), optional recommendation and English scores if needed; pay the USD 65 fee
Apply for financial assistance by about 1 March; final deadline about 1 May (rolling)
International credit students: pay the deposit, receive the I-20 and apply for an F-1 visa
syracuse-summer-college-2027.costs: Paid programme; tuition, housing and meal costs vary by course and format (see the Cost and Aid pages). USD 65 non-refundable application fee. Financial assistance and scholarships available by the March deadline.

tau-summer-school-advanced-epidemiology-.about:
Tel Aviv University's Advanced Epidemiology and Preventive Medicine Summer School offers short, intensive courses led by leading faculty and experts. In 2026 it ran from 12 to 22 July with three courses: Reproductive Epidemiology (sociodemographic, environmental and clinical determinants), One Health – Advanced Themes in Infectious Diseases Epidemiology, and Nutrition and Public Health. Each course lasts about a week (half-day sessions) and is worth 2 academic credit hours, so participants can combine courses.

The school suits medical, public health and life-science students, graduates and health professionals who want up-to-date training in epidemiology. Admission in 2026 was rolling, and partial scholarships were offered. The 2027 programme is expected in July again; check the page for the new course list.
highlights: 2 academic credits per one-week course
Taught by TAU School of Public Health experts
Partial scholarships available
tau-summer-school-advanced-epidemiology-.eligibility: Students (typically advanced undergraduates and graduate students) and professionals in medicine, public health, life sciences or related fields; any nationality. Check Israeli entry requirements for your passport.
how_to_apply: Check the programme page for the 2027 courses
Apply online through TAU International (rolling admissions)
Ask about partial scholarships when applying
Arrange accommodation (TAU housing may be available) and travel
tau-summer-school-advanced-epidemiology-.costs: 2026 tuition: US$900 per 2-credit course; partial scholarships available. Accommodation, travel and insurance extra.

tulane-pre-college-programs-2027.about:
Tulane University's Pre-College Programs bring high-school students to its New Orleans campus for credit-bearing and enrichment courses. Programmes include the Tulane Science Scholars Program (hands-on STEM courses for college credit), Futures in Public Health (science, policy and communication of global health issues) and Explorations in Architecture and Design; the Tulane Summer Enrichment Institute lets students explore subjects such as engineering, medicine and sports without grades, and the Newcomb Summer Session focuses on gender and social change.

Residential students live on campus for a two-week session (in 2026: 14–27 June, 28 June – 11 July, 12–25 July), taking one credit course or two enrichment courses, with evening activities and weekend excursions in New Orleans; commuters can take one-week enrichment or two-week credit courses. In 2026 applications opened in early December with a 27 February priority/international deadline, and admission is rolling until courses fill.
highlights: Credit-bearing STEM and public-health courses at a top research university
Residential college experience in New Orleans
No application fee; need-based aid, including for international credit students
tulane-pre-college-programs-2027.eligibility: High-school students: rising 9th–12th graders for enrichment courses, rising 11th–12th graders for credit courses; residential students must be at least 14. Graduating seniors are not eligible. International students welcome: TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores required if not a native English speaker; passport valid beyond the session and a US-based adult emergency contact (not an embassy) required.
how_to_apply: Join the mailing list for 2027 updates and choose residential or commuter and your course
Submit the free online application (opened 5 December in 2026) with transcript and other checklist items
International applicants: meet the priority deadline (27 February in 2026) and include English test scores
Pay the 10% deposit within two weeks of acceptance
tulane-pre-college-programs-2027.costs: 2026 tuition: commuter enrichment USD 995/week; residential enrichment USD 5,495 (2 weeks); commuter credit USD 2,595; residential credit USD 6,595 (2 weeks). No application fee. Need-based aid available (for international students, credit courses only).

uantwerp-winter-school-philosophy-dead-b.about:
Organised by the University of Antwerp's Centre for Ethics (Department of Philosophy, Faculty of Arts), this winter school (1–5 February 2027) examines the ambiguous status of dead human bodies, as object and subject, material and symbol, revered and despised, and explores the ethical, metaphysical and political implications in an international context that compares death-care practices inside and outside Belgium, including excursions.

It is designed for master's students and early-stage PhD students with a background in philosophy or death studies; familiarity with philosophical methods is required. Teaching takes place at the city-centre Stadscampus, and successful completion can earn ECTS credits and a micro-credential.
highlights: Small philosophy seminar on death and the body
Excursions on death-care practice
Low EUR 200 student fee
uantwerp-winter-school-philosophy-dead-b.eligibility: Master's and early PhD students in philosophy or death studies (philosophical background required); professionals/researchers at a higher fee; any nationality; good English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online before 9 November 2026
Receive the decision by 12 November 2026
Pay the fee and arrange travel and accommodation
uantwerp-winter-school-philosophy-dead-b.costs: Students EUR 200 (UAntwerp students EUR 50); professionals and funded researchers EUR 250. Includes course material, daily refreshments, lunch on Monday and Friday and excursion transport; travel and accommodation not included.
